1	/**
2	 * Reading the shift ledger back out of persisted session logs: one shift's
3	 * `shift/*` events folded into a record, the `environment/run` stamps the
4	 * cells of a shift left behind, and the four questions a restarting driver
5	 * asks of them — which cells are still pending, what the shift already spent,
6	 * what the district spent inside its window, and when its previous slot was.
7	 *
8	 * The typed `SessionEventMap` decides these payloads; a malformed one is
9	 * rejected at append by the invariant companions that own it, so the folds
10	 * here read committed events rather than revalidating them.
11	 *
12	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts/ledger
13	 */
14	
15	import { fleetCellKey } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
16	import type { FleetCell } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types'
17	import type { SessionEvent, SessionHeader, SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import type { ShiftCellRecord, ShiftEnd, ShiftStart } from './types.ts'
19	
20	/** One persisted session as the resume scan reads it. */
21	export interface ScannedSession {
22	  /** Stored header; `createdAt` bounds which stamps a shift may claim. */
23	  readonly meta: SessionHeader
24	  /** The stored log, oldest first. */
25	  readonly events: readonly SessionEvent[]
26	}
27	
28	/** One shift session's ledger, folded from its log. */
29	export interface ShiftLedger {
30	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
31	  /** Header creation time; a stamped cell older than it belongs to another shift instance. */
32	  readonly createdAt: number
33	  readonly start: ShiftStart
34	  /** Every `shift/cell` of the session, in log order. */
35	  readonly cells: readonly ShiftCellRecord[]
36	  /** The closing record, absent while the shift is unfinished. */
37	  readonly end?: ShiftEnd
38	  /** Time of the closing record, absent while the shift is unfinished. */
39	  readonly endedAt?: number
40	}
41	
42	/** One `environment/run` stamp the resume scan found, with its session's identity and spend. */
43	export interface StampedCell {
44	  /** Batch identity the stamp carries; a shift's cells carry its shift id. */
45	  readonly group: string
46	  readonly cell: FleetCell
47	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
48	  /** Header creation time of the session carrying the stamp. */
49	  readonly createdAt: number
50	  /** Input plus output tokens the session's log accounts for. */
51	  readonly totalTokens: number
52	}
53	
54	/** One cell whose session exists while the ledger never recorded an outcome for it. */
55	export interface ShiftOrphan {
56	  readonly cell: FleetCell
57	  /** The session the interrupted process created for the cell. */
58	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
59	}
60	
61	/** The cells a resuming process records as orphans and the cells it runs. */
62	export interface ShiftPending {
63	  /** Cells stamped by a session of this shift that the ledger never recorded, in plan order. */
64	  readonly orphans: readonly ShiftOrphan[]
65	  /** Cells that will not run again: recorded plus orphans, in plan order. */
66	  readonly done: readonly FleetCell[]
67	  /** Cells this process runs, in plan order. */
68	  readonly pending: readonly FleetCell[]
69	}
70	
71	/**
72	 * Fold one persisted session into its shift ledger.
73	 * @param session - the stored header and log.
74	 * @returns the ledger, or `undefined` when the log carries no `shift/start`
75	 *   and is therefore not a shift session.
76	 */
77	export function foldShiftLedger(session: ScannedSession): ShiftLedger | undefined {
78	  let start: ShiftStart | undefined
79	  let end: ShiftEnd | undefined
80	  let endedAt: number | undefined
81	  const cells: ShiftCellRecord[] = []
82	  for (const event of session.events) {
83	    if (event.type === 'shift/start') start = event.data
84	    else if (event.type === 'shift/cell') cells.push(event.data)
85	    else if (event.type === 'shift/end') {
86	      end = event.data
87	      endedAt = event.time
88	    }
89	  }
90	  if (start === undefined) return undefined
91	  return {
92	    sessionId: session.meta.id,
93	    createdAt: session.meta.createdAt,
94	    start,
95	    cells,
96	    ...end === undefined ? {} : { end },
97	    ...endedAt === undefined ? {} : { endedAt },
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * The grouped `environment/run` stamps of one persisted session, each carrying
103	 * the tokens that session's log accounts for. A session without a grouped
104	 * stamp belongs to no batch and is invisible to the resume scan.
105	 * @param session - the stored header and log.
106	 * @param totalTokens - the session's folded input plus output tokens.
107	 * @returns one entry per grouped stamp in the log.
108	 */
109	export function stampedCells(session: ScannedSession, totalTokens: number): StampedCell[] {
110	  return session.events.flatMap((event) => {
111	    if (event.type !== 'environment/run' || event.data.group === undefined) return []
112	    return [{
113	      group: event.data.group,
114	      cell: {
115	        environment: event.data.environmentId,
116	        model: event.data.model,
117	        repetition: event.data.repetition,
118	      },
119	      sessionId: session.meta.id,
120	      createdAt: session.meta.createdAt,
121	      totalTokens,
122	    }]
123	  })
124	}
125	
126	/**
127	 * Split a shift's plan cells into the orphans a resuming process records, the
128	 * cells that will not run again, and the cells it runs.
129	 *
130	 * A cell is done once the ledger recorded it, or once a session created at or
131	 * after the shift session carries its stamp — the second condition is what
132	 * makes the scan the authority whenever the ledger is behind, and the
133	 * `createdAt` bound is what keeps an older instance of the same plan out of
134	 * it. A stamped cell the ledger never recorded is an orphan: its session
135	 * exists, so running the cell again would put two sessions in one group at one
136	 * repetition and double-count the shift.
137	 * @param planCells - every cell of the frozen plan, in plan order.
138	 * @param ledger - the shift's folded ledger.
139	 * @param stamped - every grouped stamp the resume scan found.
140	 * @returns the orphans, the cells that will not run again, and the pending cells.
141	 */
142	export function splitPending(
143	  planCells: readonly FleetCell[],
144	  ledger: ShiftLedger,
145	  stamped: readonly StampedCell[],
146	): ShiftPending {
147	  const recorded = new Set(ledger.cells.map(record => fleetCellKey(record.cell)))
148	  const sessions = new Map(stamped
149	    .filter(entry => entry.group === ledger.start.shiftId && entry.createdAt >= ledger.createdAt)
150	    .map(entry => [fleetCellKey(entry.cell), entry.sessionId]))
151	  const orphans = planCells.flatMap((cell) => {
152	    const sessionId = sessions.get(fleetCellKey(cell))
153	    if (sessionId === undefined || recorded.has(fleetCellKey(cell))) return []
154	    return [{ cell, sessionId }]
155	  })
156	  const done = planCells.filter(cell => recorded.has(fleetCellKey(cell)) || sessions.has(fleetCellKey(cell)))
157	  const pending = planCells.filter(cell => !recorded.has(fleetCellKey(cell)) && !sessions.has(fleetCellKey(cell)))
158	  return { orphans, done, pending }
159	}
160	
161	/**
162	 * Tokens the sessions of one shift already spent.
163	 * @param stamped - every grouped stamp the resume scan found.
164	 * @param id - the shift whose sessions to sum.
165	 * @returns the summed input plus output tokens; `0` for a shift with no session yet.
166	 */
167	export function shiftSpend(stamped: readonly StampedCell[], id: string): number {
168	  return stamped
169	    .filter(entry => entry.group === id)
170	    .reduce((sum, entry) => sum + entry.totalTokens, 0)
171	}
172	
173	/**
174	 * Tokens one district's finished shifts closed with inside a trailing window.
175	 * @param ledgers - every shift ledger the resume scan folded.
176	 * @param district - the district to sum.
177	 * @param windowMs - width of the trailing window in milliseconds.
178	 * @param now - the current epoch milliseconds; the window ends here.
179	 * @returns the summed `shift/end` spend of the district inside the window.
180	 */
181	export function windowSpend(
182	  ledgers: readonly ShiftLedger[],
183	  district: string,
184	  windowMs: number,
185	  now: number,
186	): number {
187	  return ledgers
188	    .filter(ledger => ledger.start.plan.district === district
189	      && ledger.end !== undefined
190	      && (ledger.endedAt as number) >= now - windowMs)
191	    .reduce((sum, ledger) => sum + (ledger.end as ShiftEnd).spend, 0)
192	}
193	
194	/**
195	 * The latest slot one district opened.
196	 * @param ledgers - every shift ledger the resume scan folded.
197	 * @param district - the district to read.
198	 * @returns the slot time of the district's latest `shift/start`, or
199	 *   `undefined` when it has never opened one.
200	 */
201	export function previousSlot(ledgers: readonly ShiftLedger[], district: string): number | undefined {
202	  const slots = ledgers
203	    .filter(ledger => ledger.start.plan.district === district)
204	    .map(ledger => ledger.start.scheduledAt)
205	  return slots.length === 0 ? undefined : Math.max(...slots)
206	}

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Shifts: the durable driver of an unattended fleet. Each district opens a slot on its cadence, freezes what the slot runs into a content digest, and records the whole shift as `shift/*` events in the slot's own session log. That ledger is the only thing a restarted process reads: it resumes an interrupted shift under the same identity, runs exactly the cells that never started, and refuses a slot whose district has already spent its window. The [village-shifts Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-village-shifts.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: fleet
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
12	  config:
13	    workspaceRetention: remove-all
14	- id: shifts
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts'
16	  config:
17	    workspaceRoot: /var/lib/dsh/workspaces
18	    startImmediately: true
19	    districts:
20	      - district: workshop
21	        plan:
22	          environments:
23	            filter:
24	              heldOut: false
25	          models:
26	            - provider: <provider>
27	              model: <model>
28	          repetitions: 4
29	          tokenCeiling: 4000000
30	        cadence:
31	          intervalMs: 21600000
32	        spendWindow:
33	          windowMs: 86400000
34	          maxTokens: 12000000
35	```
36	
37	| Field | Meaning |
38	|---|---|
39	| `workspaceRoot` (required) | Existing absolute directory the fleet mints each cell's `cell-*` workspace under. Checked when the plugin loads, so a deployment whose disk is not mounted fails before a slot opens. |
40	| `districts` (required) | At least one district, each named once. The name reaches every cell's run stamp, so an export or a scoreboard can partition by it. |
41	| `districts[].plan.environments` | `{ ids: [...] }` in the given order, or `{ filter: { kind, heldOut } }` resolved against the registry when the slot freezes. |
42	| `districts[].plan.models` | At least one model route. The driver enumerates its own cells to compute a pending set and to digest the plan, so the routes are named here instead of taken from whatever default the composition currently selects. |
43	| `districts[].plan.repetitions` | Positive repetitions per environment and route; repetition indexes start at `0`. |
44	| `districts[].plan.tokenCeiling` (optional) | Positive input-plus-output token ceiling of one shift. A resumed shift runs under this ceiling minus what its own sessions already spent. |
45	| `districts[].cadence.intervalMs` (required) | Positive milliseconds between consecutive slots of the district. |
46	| `districts[].spendWindow` (optional) | `windowMs` and `maxTokens`: the trailing window across slots. Absent runs every slot the cadence opens. |
47	| `startImmediately` (required) | Whether a district with no slot in the ledger opens one as the process starts. `false` waits one interval first. |
48	
49	The service requires `fleet`, `sessions`, and `sessionPersistence`, and reads the environment registry the fleet itself injects; a slot that cannot reach it is refused with `SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN` rather than frozen over an empty inventory.
50	
51	## Service contract
52	
53	`ctx.shifts.start()` resumes every interrupted shift, then opens each district's due slot and arms its cadence timer. The loop runs once per process: the plugin starts it over the settled Loader tree and a second call joins the same run, so a driver can await the first slot without racing the plugin. `ctx.shifts.stop()` disarms every timer, cancels the fleet run in flight through its signal, and waits for the slots that are settling; plugin disposal calls it.
54	
55	`shiftDigest(plan)` is the SHA-256 hex over the district, the environment ids sorted by code unit after a filter is resolved against the registry, the model routes in listing order, the repetition count, and the token ceiling. The workspace root, the cadence, and the spend window are deployment choices and stay out of it: they decide what a deployment pays for, not what the shift runs. `shiftId(digest, scheduledAt)` is `shift-<digest>-<scheduledAt>`, the slot time in epoch milliseconds — so two processes computing the same slot compute the same identity without counting anything. That id is the shift session's id and the `group` on every cell's run stamp, which is how the sessions of one shift stay grouped durably.
56	
57	## The ledger
58	
59	The driver creates one session per slot and appends to it, flushing at every step so a process that dies leaves a truthful record.
60	
61	| Event | Written when | Payload |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `shift/start` | Before the shift's first cell starts | `shiftId`, `digest`, the frozen `plan`, `scheduledAt` |
64	| `shift/cell` | Once per cell, after that cell's own session is durable | `shiftId`, `cell`, the cell's `sessionId` when one exists, and an `outcome` of `reported` with its `certified` flag, `error` with the fleet's code and message, or `interrupted` |
65	| `shift/resume` | When a later process picks the shift up | `shiftId`, `done`, `pending` |
66	| `shift/skipped` | When a slot is refused; the session holds this one event and no `shift/start` | `digest`, `scheduledAt`, `reason` (`overlap` or `spend-window`) |
67	| `shift/end` | Once the shift is over | `shiftId`, `outcome` (`completed`, `ceiling`, or `stopped`), `spend`, and `cells` counted per outcome |
68	
69	The [persistence catalog](../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) carries each payload's declaration. Cost in EUR is not a shift field: it is folded from the `usage/priced` events of the cell sessions, so a published cost is always a logged fact.
70	
71	## Resume
72	
73	On start the driver lists persisted sessions, loads every shift session with a `shift/start` and no `shift/end`, and for each computes the pending cells as the plan's cells minus those the ledger already recorded, minus those whose `environment/run` stamp exists in a session created at or after the shift session's own `createdAt`. The stamp scan is what keeps the ledger honest when a process died before writing a record; the `createdAt` bound is what keeps an older instance of the same plan out of the answer.
74	
75	A cell whose session exists while the ledger never recorded it is an orphan: it is recorded as `shift/cell` with `outcome: interrupted` and never run again under the same repetition, because a second session for one cell would double-count it in every pass@k fold over the group. The crash is an outcome of the harness under test and stays an error row. The resumed shift then appends `shift/resume`, runs the pending cells through `ctx.fleet.run` under the same group and district with the plan's ceiling reduced by what its own sessions already spent, and closes with `shift/end`.
76	
77	## Cadence and refusals
78	
79	One shift per district is in flight at a time. The next slot of a district is its previous `shift/start.scheduledAt` plus `intervalMs`, read from the ledger, so a restart neither drifts nor doubles a slot; slots that passed while no process ran are not caught up and the hole stays visible in the slot arithmetic. Each firing arms the next slot before it runs the current one, so slots keep arriving on the cadence: one that lands on a still-running shift is refused with `shift/skipped { reason: overlap }` rather than delayed into it. Before a shift starts, the driver folds `shift/end.spend` over the district's slots inside `windowMs`; a start that would begin with the window exhausted is refused with `shift/skipped { reason: spend-window }` and creates no cell. The per-cell caps stay with the budget policy and the per-plan ceiling with the fleet; the window is the third layer, across plans.
80	
81	## Supervision
82	
83	The driver holds nothing in memory a restart needs, so a host supervisor restarting the process is the whole recovery story.
84	
85	```ini
86	[Unit]
87	Description=DeepSeek Harness shift driver
88	After=network-online.target
89	
90	[Service]
91	Type=simple
92	ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/dsh/lib/bin.js --config /etc/dsh/shifts.cordis.yml
93	WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/dsh
94	Restart=always
95	RestartSec=10
96	Environment=DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=/run/secrets/deepseek
97	KillSignal=SIGTERM
98	TimeoutStopSec=300
99	
100	[Install]
101	WantedBy=multi-user.target
102	```
103	
104	A container deployment uses its own restart policy instead — `docker run --restart=always --volume dsh-sessions:/var/lib/dsh/sessions --volume dsh-workspaces:/var/lib/dsh/workspaces <image>` — with both the persistence root and the workspace root on volumes that outlive the container, since the ledger is the recovery record. `TimeoutStopSec` must exceed the longest cell, because disposal cancels the run and waits for the cells that are settling; a shorter timeout turns a clean stop into orphans.
105	
106	### Runbook
107	
108	| Condition | What the ledger shows | What to do |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| The orchestrator crashed | A shift session with `shift/start` and no `shift/end`; after the restart, `shift/resume` and one or more `shift/cell` records with `outcome: interrupted` | Nothing, unless the interrupted count keeps growing: the restart resumes the shift. Repeated orphans in one district are the finding. |
111	| A model route is out past the retry budget | `shift/cell` records with `outcome: error` carrying `FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`, and a `shift/end` whose `cells.error` covers most of the plan | Stop the district (remove it from the config and restart) until the route recovers; the spend window limits what a flapping route can cost meanwhile. |
112	| The shift timer is dead | The district's latest `shift/start.scheduledAt` is more than one `intervalMs` old and no `shift/skipped` follows it | Check that the process is up and that its config still names the district; the ledger cannot tell a stopped timer from a stopped process. |
113	| The disk is full | Nothing — the ledger is what fails to be written | Alert on free space at the persistence root and the workspace root; `workspaceRetention: remove-all` on the fleet bounds the checkouts, but session logs have no retention policy yet. |
114	| A tool call hangs | Nothing — the shift stays open with no new `shift/cell` | Alert on a shift whose latest `shift/cell` is older than the expected cell duration; the tool-timeout policy bounds a call the executor can see, not one the provider never answers. |
115	
116	## Model Experience
117	
118	None, as the shift driver only schedules fleet runs; the environment runner owns every model-visible effect of each cell, and no `shift/*` event ever enters a model request.
119	
120	#### KV Cache effect
121	
122	None; the driver neither adds to nor changes any model request, and the shift session it writes carries no message the surface projects.
123	
124	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
125	
126	- **The ledger is not folded into a scoreboard** — a shift's rows are read by hand from the `shift/*` events until the scorekeeper folds them; a district column on a scoreboard row and one row per shift do not exist yet.
127	- **`verify-village-composition` does not name the driver** — a shift composition that lacks persistence fails on the fleet's own village rule, so the diagnostic points at the fleet entry rather than at the driver whose ledger the missing backend would drop.
128	- **Session logs have no retention policy** — workspace retention bounds the checkouts, but a deployment running for months grows its persistence root without limit, and the resume scan reads every session in it once per slot with a spend window.
129	- **A slot is refused, never queued** — a slot that arrives on a running shift, or on an exhausted spend window, leaves a `shift/skipped` and is gone; nothing re-opens it when the shift ends or the window rolls forward.
130	- **The cadence reads the host clock** — a clock jump moves a slot and never doubles one, because the ledger decides, but a district whose host clock runs backwards past a whole interval opens its next slot late.

=== driver.ts ===
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Test driver: boot the shift-driver composition, run the district's due slot
 * to completion, and print every shift ledger plus the run stamps the cells
 * left in the persistence root.
 *
 * With `DSH_TEST_SHIFT_KILL_AFTER_CELL` set, the driver instead stays up like
 * an unattended process and exits hard on the first announced cell, leaving a
 * shift whose ledger is open and whose first cell has a session but no record —
 * exactly the state the next boot resumes.
 */

import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
import type { SessionPersistence } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts'

/** Exit code the kill switch leaves behind, distinct from every clean exit. */
const KILLED = 9

/** One shift session's ledger as the e2e asserts on it. */
interface LedgerLine {
  readonly sessionId: string
  readonly events: { readonly type: string; readonly data: unknown }[]
}

/** One cell session's run stamp as the e2e asserts on it. */
interface StampLine {
  readonly sessionId: string
  readonly group?: string
  readonly district?: string
  readonly environmentId: string
  readonly repetition: number
}

const configPath = process.argv[2]
if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('shift-driver requires a config path')

/** Every shift ledger and every grouped run stamp in the persistence root. */
async function readRoot(persistence: SessionPersistence): Promise<{ ledgers: LedgerLine[]; stamps: StampLine[] }> {
  const ledgers: LedgerLine[] = []
  const stamps: StampLine[] = []
  for (const stored of await persistence.list()) {
    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(stored.id)
    const shiftEvents = events.filter((event: SessionEvent) => event.type.startsWith('shift/'))
    if (shiftEvents.length > 0) {
      ledgers.push({ sessionId: stored.id, events: shiftEvents.map(event => ({ type: event.type, data: event.data })) })
    }
    for (const event of events) {
      if (event.type !== 'environment/run') continue
      stamps.push({
        sessionId: stored.id,
        ...event.data.group === undefined ? {} : { group: event.data.group },
        ...event.data.district === undefined ? {} : { district: event.data.district },
        environmentId: event.data.environmentId,
        repetition: event.data.repetition,
      })
    }
  }
  return { ledgers, stamps }
}

const ctx = await boot('shift-driver-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
try {
  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; a slot freezes its plan against the
  // environment registry, so the driver drives only the settled application.
  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
  const shifts = ctx.get('shifts')
  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
  if (shifts === undefined || persistence === undefined) throw new Error('shift-driver requires the shifts and session persistence services')
  if (process.env.DSH_TEST_SHIFT_KILL_AFTER_CELL === '1') {
    // Registered before the shift's own observer, so the process dies before
    // the ledger records the cell whose session is already durable.
    ctx.on('fleet/cell', () => {
      process.exit(KILLED)
    })
    await shifts.start()
    // An unattended driver stays up on its cadence; the kill switch ends it.
    await new Promise<never>(() => {})
  }
  await shifts.start()
  const observed = await readRoot(persistence)
  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', ...observed })}\n`)
} finally {
  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
}

- id: cli-mock-llm
  name: '../cli-mock-llm.ts'

- id: subprocess

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

- id: goal

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
  config:

    maxTextChars: 2048

- id: environments

- id: register-environments
  name: '../environment-run/register-environments.ts'

- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: cli-mock
    model: cli-mock

- id: environment-runner

120	const RESERVATION_KEY = '<reservation>'

122	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one script per check. */

124	/** Reservation file holding the standard the current attempt measures. */

132	/**
133	 * Absolute path of one check's reserved script, refusing a check id that is not

135	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
136	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the script's file name.
137	 * @returns the absolute script path.
138	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the id or the resulting path is unusable.
139	 */

141	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {

144	  const script = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)

151	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
152	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
153	  try {
154	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
155	  } catch {
156	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.

161	/** SHA-256 over every regular file under a directory: relative POSIX path, then bytes, in sorted order. */
162	async function hashDirectory(root: string): Promise<string> {
163	  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
164	  const files = entries.filter(entry => entry.isFile()).map(entry => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).sort()
165	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
166	  for (const file of files) {
167	    hash.update(relative(root, file).split(sep).join('/')).update('\0').update(await readFile(file)).update('\0')
168	  }
169	  return hash.digest('hex')

172	/** What one check-owned path digests to when nothing is there to read. */
173	const ABSENT_DIGEST = 'absent'

175	/**
176	 * SHA-256 over one check-owned path: its tree when a directory, its bytes when
177	 * a file, and {@link ABSENT_DIGEST} when it is gone. Deleting a declared path
178	 * is as much a change to the check-owned set as rewriting it.
179	 * @param path - absolute path to digest.
180	 * @returns the digest, or the absent marker.
181	 */
182	async function hashCheckOwnedPath(path: string): Promise<string> {
183	  if (await isDirectory(path)) return hashDirectory(path)
184	  try {
185	    return createHash('sha256').update(await readFile(path)).digest('hex')
186	  } catch {
187	    // readFile rejects for a missing or unreadable path; either way the run
188	    // cannot read what the fixture supplied, which is the change to record.
189	    return ABSENT_DIGEST
190	  }
191	}

193	/**
194	 * SHA-256 over the whole check-owned set: the validator's reserved directory,
195	 * when a barrier minted one, and every path the environment declared immutable,
196	 * each keyed by the name it is declared under.
197	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory, which immutable paths are relative to.
198	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
199	 * @param immutable - the environment's declared immutable paths.
200	 * @returns one digest over the whole set.
201	 */
202	async function hashCheckOwned(
203	  workspace: string,
204	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
205	  immutable: readonly string[],
206	): Promise<string> {
207	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
208	  if (runDirectory !== undefined) {
209	    hash.update(RESERVATION_KEY).update('\0').update(await hashDirectory(runDirectory)).update('\0')
210	  }
211	  for (const path of immutable) {
212	    hash.update(path).update('\0').update(await hashCheckOwnedPath(join(workspace, path))).update('\0')
213	  }
214	  return hash.digest('hex')
215	}

217	/**
218	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
219	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
220	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
221	 */
222	async function prepareWorkspace(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string | undefined> {
223	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {
224	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`workspace "${workspace}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE')
225	  }
226	  if (fixture === undefined) return undefined
227	  if (!isAbsolute(fixture) || !await isDirectory(fixture)) {
228	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`fixture "${fixture}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE')
229	  }
230	  await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
231	  return hashDirectory(fixture)
232	}

234	/**
235	 * Overlay the fixture again so implementer edits to validator-owned files do
236	 * not reach the checks, then digest the workspace the validation will read.
237	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory.
238	 * @param fixture - the task fixture, absent for a task without one.
239	 * @returns the workspace digest as the validation begins.
240	 */
241	async function restoreFixture(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string> {
242	  if (fixture !== undefined) await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
243	  return hashDirectory(workspace)
244	}

246	/**
247	 * Write the attempt's standard snapshot and one script per active check into
248	 * the reservation, so what the checks execute lives where the implementer
249	 * cannot read it.
250	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
251	 * @param standard - the standard this attempt measures.
252	 * @returns the script path per check id; empty without a reservation.
253	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when a check id cannot name a script file.
254	 */
255	async function materializeChecks(runDirectory: string | undefined, standard: StandardView): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
256	  const scripts = new Map<string, string>()
257	  if (runDirectory === undefined) return scripts
258	  await mkdir(join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
259	  await writeFile(join(runDirectory, STANDARD_FILE), `${JSON.stringify(standard, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
260	  for (const check of standard.checks) {
261	    const script = scriptPath(runDirectory, check.id)
262	    await writeFile(script, `${check.run}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
263	    scripts.set(check.id, script)
264	  }
265	  return scripts
266	}

268	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
269	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
270	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
271	}
272	
273	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
274	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
275	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
276	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
277	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
278	  const marker = '\n…'
279	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
280	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
281	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
282	}
283	
284	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
285	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
286	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
287	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
288	  const lines = [`${exit}${cause}`]
289	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
290	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
291	  return bound(lines.join('\n'), maxChars)
292	}
293	
294	/** One directive per failed run: the count as root cause, the evidence as detail, never the checks themselves. */
295	function describeFailures(failures: readonly CheckResult[], maxChars: number): DirectiveRequest {
296	  return {
297	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
298	    detail: bound(failures.map((failure, index) => `${index + 1}. ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
299	  }
300	}

302	/**
303	 * The one directive a tampered attempt issues. A digest comparison knows that
304	 * the check-owned set changed and nothing else, so the text names neither a
305	 * path nor a check: it states that the measurement is void and that the run is
306	 * over. Pinned verbatim by the runner README and the `read-barrier-tamper`
307	 * snapshot.
308	 */
309	const TAMPER_DIRECTIVE: DirectiveRequest = {
310	  rootCause: 'the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt',
311	  detail: 'Those files belong to the validator: the task is to make them pass, never to change them. This run is void and no certificate can follow it.',
312	}
313	
314	/** The evidence every check of a tampered attempt records, since none of them ran. */
315	const TAMPER_EVIDENCE = 'not executed: the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt'
316	
317	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
318	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
319	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
320	}

322	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
323	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
324	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
325	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
326	  ))
327	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
328	  const total: TokenUsage = {
329	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
330	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
331	  }
332	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
333	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
334	      const value = step[key]
335	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
336	    })
337	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
338	  }
339	  return total
340	}

342	/** Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. */
343	export class EnvironmentRunner extends Service {
344	  static inject = ['environments', 'agents', 'agentDefaultModel', 'goals', 'completionStandards', 'shell', 'sessions']
345	
346	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
347	    isolation: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).required(),
348	    maxAttempts: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
349	    maxGoalRounds: z.natural().min(1),
350	    checkTimeoutMs: z.natural().min(1),
351	    evidenceMaxChars: z.natural().min(1).default(2000),
352	  })
353	
354	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
355	
356	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
357	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
358	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
359	  }
360	
361	  /**
362	   * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it.
363	   * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, district, and abort signal.
364	   * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage.
365	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable
366	   *   workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard.
367	   */
368	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
369	    const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(request.environment)
370	    if (definition === undefined) {
371	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`environment "${request.environment}" is not registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT')
372	    }
373	    const fixtureSha256 = await prepareWorkspace(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
374	    const model = request.model ?? this.defaultModel()
375	    const stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp = {
376	      kind: 'environment/run',
377	      version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
378	      environmentId: definition.id,
379	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
380	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
381	      ...environmentContentHashes(definition, fixtureSha256),
382	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
383	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
384	      ...request.district === undefined ? {} : { district: request.district },
385	      model,
386	      isolation: this.resolved.isolation,
387	    }
388	    const handle = await this.ctx.agents.create({
389	      sessionId: SessionId(`environment-${randomUUID()}`),
390	      meta: { cwd: request.workspace },
391	      agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
392	      ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
393	      setup: (agentCtx) => {
394	        installModelSelection(agentCtx, { current: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model }, assembled: undefined })
395	      },
396	    })
397	    try {
398	      return await this.drive(handle.agent, definition, stamp, request)
399	    } finally {
400	      await handle.dispose()
401	    }
402	  }

404	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
405	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
406	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
407	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
408	  }
409	
410	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
411	  private async drive(
412	    agent: Agent,
413	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
414	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
415	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
416	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
417	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
418	    await agent.whenIdle()
419	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
420	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
421	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
422	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
423	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
424	    })
425	    goals.disarm(agent)
426	    const authored = completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
427	    const immutable = definition.task.immutable ?? []
428	    // Stock the reservation and digest the check-owned set before the
429	    // implementer's first turn: that digest is what every later attempt is
430	    // compared against.
431	    await materializeChecks(runDirectory, authored)
432	    let checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
433	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
434	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
435	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
436	    try {
437	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
438	        await this.deliver(agent, prompt)
439	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
440	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }

448	        // is the baseline the next attempt must still find.
449	        checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
450	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts)
451	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
452	          executor: 'runner',
453	          treeHash,
454	        })
455	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
456	        if (outcome.certified) {

458	          const current = goals.get(agent)
459	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
460	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')

462	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })

465	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)

475	      sessionId: agent.id,
476	      stamp,
477	      attempts,
478	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
479	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
480	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
481	    }
482	  }

484	  /** Send one user turn to the implementer and wait for the whole agent to go idle. */

490	  /**
491	   * Record one attempt whose check-owned set changed under the validator. The
492	   * checks are not executed — the workspace no longer measures the task — so
493	   * every result records that, the run is recorded as `tampered` and certifies
494	   * nothing, and the implementer receives the tamper directive as its last
495	   * validation follow-up before the attempt loop ends.
496	   * @param agent - the implementer whose attempt this is.
497	   * @param standard - the standard the attempt would have measured.
498	   * @param ref - that standard's exact revision.
499	   * @param workspace - the run's workspace, digested as the attempt left it.
500	   * @param attempt - one-based attempt number.
501	   * @returns the attempt the report carries.
502	   */
503	  private async recordTamper(
504	    agent: Agent,
505	    standard: StandardView,
506	    ref: StandardRef,
507	    workspace: string,
508	    attempt: number,
509	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunAttempt> {
510	    const results: CheckResult[] = standard.checks.map(check => ({
511	      checkId: check.id,
512	      status: 'fail',
513	      evidence: bound(TAMPER_EVIDENCE, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
514	    }))
515	    const treeHash = await hashDirectory(workspace)
516	    this.ctx.completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
517	      executor: 'runner',
518	      treeHash,
519	      tampered: true,
520	    })
521	    this.ctx.completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, TAMPER_DIRECTIVE)
522	    await this.deliver(agent, followupText(TAMPER_DIRECTIVE))
523	    return { attempt, results, treeHash }
524	  }

526	  /** The standard the run measures; the implementer cannot mutate it, so another goal's standard or none is an anomaly. */
527	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
528	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
529	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {
530	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the standard for goal "${goalId}" is no longer current`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST')
531	    }
532	    return standard
533	  }
534	
535	  /**
536	   * Reserve the run's validator-owned directory and stock what the checks read
537	   * from it. Without a composed barrier there is no reservation and the checks
538	   * run their instructions inline, exactly as the run's declared isolation says.
539	   * @param agent - the implementer agent this run drives.
540	   * @param definition - the environment being run, supplying the held-out fixture.
541	   * @returns the reservation, or `undefined` when no barrier is composed.
542	   */
543	  private async reserve(agent: Agent, definition: EnvironmentDefinition): Promise<string | undefined> {
544	    const barrier = this.ctx.get('readBarrier')
545	    if (barrier === undefined) return undefined
546	    const runDirectory = barrier.reserve(agent)
547	    // A held-out environment's fixture is evaluation material: the copy under
548	    // the reservation is the one an inspecting validator reads, never the
549	    // workspace overlay the implementer works in.
550	    if (definition.heldOut && definition.task.fixture !== undefined) {

556	  /**

558	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
559	   * instruction inline.
560	   */
561	  private async execute(
562	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
563	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
564	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
565	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
566	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
567	    for (const check of checks) {
568	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
569	      const spec = this.ctx.shell.resolve({
570	        command: script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`,
571	        workdir: request.workspace,
572	        timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
573	        signal: request.signal,
574	      })
575	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(spec)
576	      results.push({
577	        checkId: check.id,
578	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
579	        evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
580	      })
581	    }
582	    return results
583	  }

84	/**
85	 * Light last-wins fold of the `goal` projection unit. Unlike the strict
86	 * replay fold (fold.ts: transition validation, fail-loud on malformed
87	 * changes, Set-typed state), this transition is projection-grade: the state
88	 * is plain JSON (persisted-cache precondition), any non-goal or malformed
89	 * event returns the same reference (the registry's Object.is gate — the
90	 * title/todos posture), and correctness of the written change is the write
91	 * side's job (GoalService validated it before appending; the package
92	 * invariant rejects a violating stream fail-loud where it is installed).
93	 * @param state - the projection covering all prior events.
94	 * @param event - the next committed session event.
95	 * @returns the next projection (same reference when the event is not a goal change).
96	 */
97	export function applyGoalProjection(state: GoalProjection | null, event: SessionEvent): GoalProjection | null {
98	  if (event.type !== 'goal/change') return state
99	  let change: GoalChangeMeta | undefined
100	  try {
101	    change = decodeGoalChange(event.data)
102	  } catch (_invalidPersistedGoalChange) {
103	    return state
104	  }
105	  if (change === undefined) return state
106	  return change.operation === 'clear'
107	    ? null
108	    : {
109	      goal: change.goal,
110	      roundsStarted: change.roundsStarted,
111	      createdAt: change.createdAt,
112	      updatedAt: change.updatedAt,
113	    }
114	}

142	/** Validate a caller-visible positive safe-integer round cap. */
143	function resolveMaxGoalRounds(value: number): number {
144	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value < 1) {
145	    throw new GoalError('maxGoalRounds must be a positive safe integer', 'GOAL_INVALID_MAX_ROUNDS')
146	  }
147	  return value
148	}

150	/** Validate and normalize an objective at the domain boundary. */
151	function resolveObjective(value: string): string {
152	  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim().length === 0) {
153	    throw new GoalError('goal objective must be a non-empty string', 'GOAL_INVALID_OBJECTIVE')
154	  }
155	  return value.trim()
156	}

159	function resolveCreateGoal(request: CreateGoalRequest, defaultMaxGoalRounds: number): ResolvedCreateGoal {
160	  return {
161	    objective: resolveObjective(request.objective),
162	    maxGoalRounds: resolveMaxGoalRounds(request.maxGoalRounds ?? defaultMaxGoalRounds),
163	  }

166	/** Validate and detach one policy-owned blocker explanation. */
167	function resolveBlockReason(reason: unknown): GoalBlockReason {
168	  const record = typeof reason === 'object' && reason !== null && !Array.isArray(reason)
169	    ? reason as Record<string, unknown>
170	    : undefined
171	  const code = record?.['code']
172	  const message = record?.['message']
173	  if (typeof code !== 'string' || !/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/.test(code)
174	    || typeof message !== 'string' || message.trim().length === 0) {
175	    throw new GoalError(
176	      'goal block reason requires a lower-kebab-case code and a non-empty message',
177	      'GOAL_INVALID_BLOCK_REASON',
178	    )
179	  }
180	  return { code, message: message.trim() }
181	}

478	    ref: GoalRef,

480	    allowed: readonly GoalPhase[],
481	    phase: GoalPhase,

485	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)

488	      const snapshot = { ...current }
489	      for (const guard of this.completionGuards) guard(agent, snapshot)

491	    return this.commitCurrent(agent, cache, operation, this.withPhase(current, phase), activation)

502	  /** Commit a mutation that retains the current goal's derived counters/times. */
503	  private commitCurrent(

505	    cache: GoalCache,
506	    operation: Exclude<GoalOperation, 'create' | 'clear'>,
507	    goal: GoalSnapshot,
508	    activation: GoalActivation,
509	  ): GoalView {
510	    const createdAt = cache.state.createdAt
511	    /* v8 ignore next -- strict replay and every snapshot commit set createdAt whenever a current goal exists */
512	    if (createdAt === undefined) throw new Error('current goal cache lacks createdAt')
513	    return this.commitSnapshot(
514	      agent,
515	      cache,
516	      operation,
517	      goal,
518	      cache.state.roundsStarted,
519	      createdAt,
520	      this.nextMutationTime(cache),
521	      activation,
522	    )
523	  }

525	  /** Clamp a current goal's next timestamp across backward wall-clock movement. */
526	  private nextMutationTime(cache: GoalCache): number {
527	    const updatedAt = cache.state.updatedAt
528	    /* v8 ignore next -- strict replay and every snapshot commit set updatedAt whenever a current goal exists */
529	    if (updatedAt === undefined) throw new Error('current goal cache lacks updatedAt')
530	    return Math.max(Date.now(), updatedAt)

2	 * Session budget guard. Configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps are
3	 * measured against the durable session log before every proposed step; the
4	 * first cap the log exceeds is recorded as a `budget/breach` event, blocks any
5	 * active goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every
6	 * step served by a priced route also gets a durable `usage/priced` record, so

55	/**

89	/** The caps a validated configuration actually enforces, paired with their values. */
90	interface ResolvedConfig {
91	  readonly caps: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[]
92	  readonly pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
93	  /** Whether {@link pricing} names any route; an empty table never reads the log. */
94	  readonly prices: boolean

99	/** Reject a cap that cannot express a ceiling before any session depends on it. */
100	function requireFiniteCap(cap: BudgetCapId, value: number): void {
101	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
102	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: ${cap} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
103	  }
104	}
105	
106	/** Reject a rate that cannot price a route before any session depends on it. */
107	function requireFiniteRate(route: string, field: keyof BudgetRoutePricing, value: number): void {
108	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
109	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: pricing["${route}"].${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
110	  }
111	}

113	/**
114	 * Validate one deployment configuration and materialize the enforced caps.
115	 * Every rejection happens at plugin load, before a session can depend on a cap
116	 * the policy could not enforce.
117	 */
118	function resolveBudgetConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
119	  // The schema defaulted the table — the cast records that runtime fact.
120	  const pricing = config.pricing as Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
121	  for (const [route, rates] of Object.entries(pricing)) {
122	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'inputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens)
123	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'outputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
124	  }
125	  const prices = Object.keys(pricing).length > 0
126	  if (config.maxCostEur !== undefined && !prices) {
127	    throw new TypeError('budget-policy: maxCostEur needs a non-empty pricing table; an unpriced route has no cost cap')
128	  }
129	  const caps: (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] = []
130	  for (const cap of CAP_ORDER) {
131	    const value = config[cap]
132	    if (value === undefined) continue
133	    requireFiniteCap(cap, value)
134	    caps.push([cap, value])
135	  }
136	  return { caps, pricing, prices, pricingDigest: pricingTableDigest(pricing) }
137	}

139	/**
140	 * Build the durable price of one accounted message at the configured rates.
141	 * @param event - a message {@link unpricedUsage} selected, so its route is priced.
142	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
143	 * @returns the record to append for that step.
144	 */
145	function priceMessage(event: AccountedMessage, resolved: ResolvedConfig): UsagePriced {
146	  const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
147	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-non-null-assertion -- unpricedUsage yields only routes the table names
148	  const rates = resolved.pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]!
149	  const inputTokens = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
150	  const outputTokens = event.data.usage.outputTokens
151	  return {
152	    turn: event.data.turn,
153	    step: event.data.step,
154	    provider,
155	    model,
156	    inputTokens,
157	    outputTokens,
158	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens,
159	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens,
160	    costEur: costEurFor(inputTokens, outputTokens, rates),
161	    pricingDigest: resolved.pricingDigest,
162	  }
163	}

165	/**
166	 * Record the price of every priced-route step the log does not price yet. The
167	 * selection is log-derived, so a resumed session prices what its predecessor
168	 * left unpriced and a second call over the same log appends nothing.
169	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log is priced.
170	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
171	 */
172	function priceUnpricedSteps(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): void {
173	  if (!resolved.prices) return
174	  for (const event of unpricedUsage(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)) {
175	    agent.session.append('usage/priced', priceMessage(event, resolved))
176	  }
177	}

179	/**
180	 * Measure the session log against the enforced caps.
181	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log carries the spend.
182	 * @param resolved - the caps and pricing this deployment enforces.
183	 * @returns the first breach in {@link CAP_ORDER}, or `undefined` while every cap holds.
184	 */
185	function detectBreach(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): BudgetBreach | undefined {
186	  if (resolved.caps.length === 0) return undefined
187	  const spend = foldBudgetSpend(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)
188	  for (const [cap, limit] of resolved.caps) {
189	    const measured = measuredFor(spend, cap)
190	    if (measured > limit) return { cap, measured, limit }
191	  }
192	  return undefined
193	}

195	/**
196	 * Block the session's goal so no goal-round driver continues it. The goal
197	 * domain is optional: a composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current
198	 * goal, or whose goal already left the `active` phase still gets the durable
199	 * breach record and the stopped turn.
200	 */
201	function blockGoal(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, breach: BudgetBreach): void {
202	  const goals = ctx.get('goals')
203	  if (goals === undefined) return
204	  const goal = goals.get(agent)
205	  if (goal === undefined || goal.phase !== 'active') return
206	  goals.block(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision }, {
207	    code: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED,
208	    message: `Session budget ${breach.cap} exceeded: ${breach.measured} of ${breach.limit}.`,
209	  })
210	}

212	/**
213	 * Register the pre-step budget check and the pricing records for the lifetime
214	 * of `ctx`.
215	 * @param ctx - plugin context; both listeners are disposed with it.
216	 * @param config - the per-session caps and pricing to enforce.
217	 * @throws {TypeError} when the configuration cannot express the caps it declares.
218	 */
219	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
220	  const resolved = resolveBudgetConfig(config)
221	
222	  // Prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build
223	  // request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run.
224	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
225	    // Priced before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is
226	    // priced by the same step that records the breach.
227	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
228	    const breach = detectBreach(agent, resolved)
229	    if (breach === undefined) return next()
230	    agent.session.append('budget/breach', breach)
231	    blockGoal(ctx, agent, breach)
232	    return { kind: 'reject' }
233	  }, { prepend: true })
234	
235	  // A turn that closes normally opens no further step, so its final message is
236	  // priced at the stop boundary instead.
237	  ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping', ({ agent }) => {
238	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
239	  })
240	}

34	/** Validate one recorded breach against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
35	function validateBreach(
36	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
37	  breach: BudgetBreach,
38	  fail: InvariantFailure,
39	): void {
40	  const { cap, measured, limit } = breach
41	  if (!(measured > limit)) {
42	    fail(`budget/breach records ${cap} measured ${measured} which does not exceed its limit ${limit}`)
43	  }
44	  // Cost is priced from configuration the log does not carry, so only the
45	  // log-derived caps are recomputable here.
46	  if (cap === 'maxCostEur') return
47	  const recomputed = measuredFor(foldBudgetSpend(prior, {}), cap)
48	  if (recomputed !== measured) {
49	    fail(`budget/breach records ${cap} measured ${measured}, but folding the preceding events yields ${recomputed}`)
50	  }
51	}

53	/** Validate one recorded price against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
54	function validatePriced(
55	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
56	  priced: UsagePriced,
57	  fail: InvariantFailure,
58	): void {
59	  const step = `turn ${priced.turn} step ${priced.step}`
60	  for (const earlier of prior) {
61	    if (earlier.type !== 'usage/priced') continue
62	    if (earlier.data.turn !== priced.turn || earlier.data.step !== priced.step) continue
63	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${step}, which seq ${earlier.seq} already priced`)
64	  }
65	  const cited = prior.find((event): event is SessionEvent<'assistant/message'> =>
66	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.turn === priced.turn && event.data.step === priced.step)
67	  if (cited === undefined) return fail(`usage/priced prices ${step}, which no preceding assistant/message reports`)
68	  const usage = cited.data.usage
69	  if (usage === undefined
70	    || billedInputTokens(usage) !== priced.inputTokens
71	    || usage.outputTokens !== priced.outputTokens) {
72	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${priced.inputTokens} input and ${priced.outputTokens} output tokens for ${step}, which its assistant/message does not report`)
73	  }
74	  const { provider, model } = cited.data.message.source
75	  if (provider !== priced.provider || model !== priced.model) {
76	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${step} on route ${routeKey(priced.provider, priced.model)}, which its assistant/message reports as ${routeKey(provider, model)}`)
77	  }
78	  const recomputed = costEurFor(priced.inputTokens, priced.outputTokens, priced)
79	  if (recomputed !== priced.costEur) {
80	    fail(`usage/priced records costEur ${priced.costEur} for ${step}, but its own rates price its own tokens at ${recomputed}`)
81	  }
82	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure session-log folds behind every budget decision: the spend a cap is
3	 * measured against, and the steps whose price the log does not yet state. The
4	 * policy plugin and the invariant companion both read through them, so a
5	 * recorded breach or price is recomputable from the same events by anyone
6	 * holding the log.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
9	 */
10	
11	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
14	import type { AccountedMessage, BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing, BudgetSpend } from './types.ts'
15	
16	/** The key one step is identified by within its own session log. */
17	function stepKey(turn: number, step: number): string {
18	  return `${turn}/${step}`
19	}
20	
21	/** Whether one event is an assistant message the provider reported accounting for. */
22	function isAccounted(event: SessionEvent): event is AccountedMessage {
23	  return event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Fold billed spend and elapsed wall time out of one session log.
28	 *
29	 * Only `assistant/message` carries a step's final provider accounting, so it is
30	 * the single usage source: the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the
31	 * same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. Each message
32	 * prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid
33	 * session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it;
34	 * a route absent from `pricing` contributes tokens but no cost.
35	 *
36	 * @param events - the session events to fold, oldest first.
37	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
38	 * @returns the spend measured over exactly those events.
39	 */
40	export function foldBudgetSpend(
41	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
42	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
43	): BudgetSpend {
44	  let inputTokens = 0
45	  let outputTokens = 0
46	  let costEur = 0
47	  for (const event of events) {
48	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
49	    const input = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
50	    inputTokens += input
51	    outputTokens += event.data.usage.outputTokens
52	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
53	    const rates = pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]
54	    if (rates === undefined) continue
55	    costEur += costEurFor(input, event.data.usage.outputTokens, rates)
56	  }
57	  const first = events[0]
58	  const last = events[events.length - 1]
59	  return {
60	    inputTokens,
61	    outputTokens,
62	    totalTokens: inputTokens + outputTokens,
63	    wallMs: first === undefined || last === undefined ? 0 : last.time - first.time,
64	    costEur,
65	  }
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Select the priced-route steps the log does not yet state a price for.
70	 *
71	 * The selection is a function of the log alone, so a resumed session prices
72	 * exactly the steps its predecessor left unpriced and never prices one twice: a
73	 * step is skipped once any `usage/priced` in the log carries its turn and step.
74	 * A message without provider accounting, and a message on a `provider/model`
75	 * the table does not name, are both skipped — an unpriced route has no rate to
76	 * record.
77	 *
78	 * @param events - the session events to read, oldest first.
79	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
80	 * @returns the messages awaiting a durable price, in log order.
81	 */
82	export function unpricedUsage(
83	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
84	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
85	): readonly AccountedMessage[] {
86	  const priced = new Set<string>()
87	  for (const event of events) {
88	    if (event.type !== 'usage/priced') continue
89	    priced.add(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))
90	  }
91	  const pending: AccountedMessage[] = []
92	  for (const event of events) {
93	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
94	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
95	    if (pricing[routeKey(provider, model)] === undefined) continue
96	    if (priced.has(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))) continue
97	    pending.push(event)
98	  }
99	  return pending
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * Read the spend one cap is measured against.
104	 * @param spend - folded session spend.
105	 * @param cap - the cap whose measurement is wanted.
106	 * @returns the measured value for that cap.
107	 */
108	export function measuredFor(spend: BudgetSpend, cap: BudgetCapId): number {
109	  switch (cap) {
110	    case 'maxInputTokens':
111	      return spend.inputTokens
112	    case 'maxOutputTokens':
113	      return spend.outputTokens
114	    case 'maxTotalTokens':
115	      return spend.totalTokens
116	    case 'maxWallMs':
117	      return spend.wallMs
118	    case 'maxCostEur':
119	      return spend.costEur
120	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- BudgetCapId is closed and every member is handled above */
121	    default:
122	      return assertNever(cap, 'budget cap measurement')
123	  }
124	}
